close_reason: Updated the stale 'structural clone' comment on verify_delta_crl_and_collect to reflect the post-cache state (delta_crl borrows from self.delta_crl). Refactor to return Option<&[RevokedCert]> noted as a feasible follow-up perf cleanup; not done in this pass to keep scope minimal.
description:
## Location
pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs lines 567-582 (verify_delta_crl_and_collect return statement).

## Finding
The function ends with this comment block:

```
// NOTE: The clone here is a structural requirement. Returning &[RevokedCert]
// (Option A) is not possible because delta_crl is a caller-local variable; a
// reference into it cannot outlive the if let block at both call sites without
// a significant lifetime refactor of check_revocation and
// check_revocation_against_anchor. A borrow-based design would require either
// pre-parsing the delta CRL into self at construction time (deferred to v0.3
// caching work) or passing the parsed CertificateList in from the caller and
// restructuring both call sites. ...
Ok(delta_crl
    .tbs_cert_list
    .revoked_certificates
    .clone()
    .unwrap_or_default())
```

The claim 'delta_crl is a caller-local variable' was correct under the pre-cache design where each check_revocation call decoded delta_crl_der locally. The pass-1/pass-2 parse-once refactor removed that locality: self.delta_crl: Option<CertificateList> is now stored in the struct, and at both call sites delta_crl: &CertificateList is borrowed via &self.delta_crl (pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:309 and :433). The borrow lives as long as &self, which outlives the function call.

This means the comment's stated rationale ('caller-local') is stale and the function could now legitimately return Option<&[RevokedCert]> to avoid the clone. The comment also explicitly anticipates this future state: 'A borrow-based design would require ... pre-parsing the delta CRL into self at construction time (deferred to v0.3 caching work)' — but pre-parsing has already happened. The comment was not updated when the cache landed.

## Why this matters
Stale comments mislead future maintainers. A reader who trusts this comment would believe the clone is structurally required (it is not) and skip the available perf improvement. The clone allocates a fresh Vec<RevokedCert> on every check_revocation call when a delta CRL is configured.

## Severity
P3 (idiom / opinion / minor perf):
- Documentation accuracy is a code-review concern, not a correctness issue.
- The clone bound is small (proportional to delta CRL size, typically tens of entries) and runs once per check call.
- Touching this requires a coordinated lifetime refactor at both call sites in CrlChecker.

## Fix options
1. Minimal: update the comment to remove the 'caller-local' claim and document the actual reason for the clone (e.g., 'returning Option<&[RevokedCert]> would require restructuring both call sites; deferred as low-priority cleanup').
2. Idiomatic: refactor the function to return Option<&[RevokedCert]>, restructure call sites to consume the borrow before self.delta_crl goes out of scope. Avoids one clone per call. This is what the comment originally promised would be possible 'in v0.3 caching work' — that work has landed.

Either is acceptable; the stale comment must not remain as-is.
title: (IDIOM) P3: stale 'structural clone' comment in verify_delta_crl_and_collect after parse-once cache landed
